unit_description: This unit uses arrays and number lines to represent multiplication. Students build arrays, write two multiplication equations for an array, and connect models, equations, and stories.
unit_goals: Write two multiplication equations for an array.
Represent multiplication on a number line.
Use the commutative property with arrays.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students build arrays for multiplication, write two equations for each array, and show multiplication as jumps on a number line.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting rows and columns in arrays.
lessons.concept: An array is a set of objects arranged in equal rows and columns. The number of rows and columns are the factors, and the total is the product.
lessons.practice: Build arrays and write matching multiplication equations.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by looking at arrays.

questions.prompt: An array has 3 rows and 4 columns. How many items are there?
How many rows are in a 2 by 6 array?
questions.hint: The first number is the number of rows.

questions.prompt: How many columns are in a 5 by 3 array?
questions.hint: The second number is the number of columns.

learn.title: Build Arrays to Represent Multiplication
teaching_points: An array has rows and columns.
Rows go across; columns go up and down.
Multiply rows times columns to find the total.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Build an array for 4 × 3 and find the total.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw an array for each multiplication expression and write the total.

flashcards.title: Array Vocabulary
flashcards.instructions: Review array, row, and column words.

bigIdea.title: Build Arrays to Represent Multiplication
bigIdea.subtitle: Rows and columns show multiplication
bigIdea.intro: An array is like a grid. The number of rows and columns are the factors, and the total number of items is the product.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does an array show the two factors of a multiplication problem?

ruleCards.description: Columns go up and down the array.

lessons.lesson_title: Write Two Multiplication Equations for an Array
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting rows and columns and writing two equations.
lessons.concept: An array can be seen two ways: rows × columns or columns × rows. Both give the same product because of the commutative property.
lessons.practice: Write two multiplication equations for each array and explain why they have the same product.
lessons.objective: Write two multiplication equations for an array.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by writing two equations.

questions.prompt: Write two equations for 2 rows of 6.

learn.title: Write Two Multiplication Equations for an Array

example.prompt: Write two equations for an array with 3 rows and 6 columns.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Write two equations for an array with 4 rows and 5 columns.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Write two multiplication equations for each array.

flashcards.title: Commutative Property
flashcards.instructions: Review the commutative property of multiplication.

bigIdea.title: Write Two Multiplication Equations for an Array
bigIdea.subtitle: An array can be turned two ways
bigIdea.intro: Turn your head and an array looks different, but the total stays the same. That is why 3 × 6 and 6 × 3 both equal 18.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why can you write two equations for the same array?

ruleCards.description: Count the rows first, then the columns.
Count the columns first, then the rows.

lessons.lesson_title: Represent Multiplication on a Number Line
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by making equal jumps on a number line.
lessons.concept: A number line can show multiplication as equal jumps. 4 × 3 is four jumps of 3, landing on 12.
lessons.practice: Draw jumps on a number line for multiplication facts.
lessons.objective: Represent multiplication on a number line.

questions.prompt: Make 3 jumps of 4. Where do you land?
What multiplication equation matches 2 jumps of 6?

learn.title: Represent Multiplication on a Number Line
teaching_points: The number of jumps is one factor.
The size of each jump is the other factor.
Where you land is the product.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Show 3 × 5 on a number line and find the product.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw equal jumps on a number line for each multiplication expression.

bigIdea.title: Represent Multiplication on a Number Line
bigIdea.subtitle: Jumps show equal groups
bigIdea.intro: On a number line, multiplication looks like equal jumps. The number of jumps and the size of each jump are the two factors.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is a number-line jump like an equal group?

ruleCards.description: The first factor tells how many jumps to make.
The second factor tells how far each jump is.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by matching arrays, equations, and word problems.
lessons.concept: A multiplication story can be shown as an array, a number line, or an equation. All three represent the same multiplication.
lessons.practice: Match and create models, equations, and stories for multiplication.
lessons.objective: Connect models, equations, and stories for multiplication.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by matching models to equations.

questions.prompt: A number line has 4 jumps of 3. What is the product?

learn.title: Connect Models, Equations, and Stories
teaching_points: The same multiplication can be shown in different ways.
A picture, equation, and story should all match.
Models help explain the meaning of multiplication.

example.prompt: Show 3 × 4 as an array, a number line, and a story.
example.equation: Array: 3 rows of 4. Number line: 3 jumps of 4. Story: 3 bags of 4 apples.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Match the story to a model: 5 boxes with 6 crayons each.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw a model, write an equation, and tell a story for each multiplication.

flashcards.title: Models and Stories
flashcards.instructions: Review how models, equations, and stories connect.

bigIdea.title: Connect Models, Equations, and Stories
bigIdea.subtitle: Multiplication can look different but mean the same thing
bigIdea.intro: A multiplication problem can be shown as an array, jumps on a number line, or a story. All of them show the same factors and product.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is it useful to show multiplication in different ways?

ruleCards.description: Rows and columns show the factors and the total.
Equal jumps show the same multiplication as an array.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of arrays, two equations, number lines, and connecting models.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: building arrays, writing two equations, number-line multiplication, and connecting models, equations, and stories.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about multiplication models.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: Write two equations for an array with 5 rows and 3 columns.
What is 4 jumps of 5 on a number line?
A story says 3 boxes of 8 crayons. What is the total?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: arrays + two equations + number line + models = multiplication models

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which equation matches an array of 4 rows and 7 columns?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 10 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 10 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Multiplication Models
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: arrays, two equations for an array, number-line multiplication, and connecting models, equations, and stories.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about multiplication models?

ruleCards.description: Rows and columns give two factors for the same array.
Multiplication can be shown as equal jumps on a number line.
